title: Depressive disorder (depression) - WHO fact sheet
text: Depression is a common mental disorder. WHO estimates that around 5% of adults worldwide live with depression at any given time, and more women are affected than men.

title: Depressive disorder (depression) - WHO fact sheet
text: Typical features include persistent low mood, loss of interest or pleasure in previously enjoyable activities, low energy, poor concentration, disturbed sleep or appetite, and feelings of guilt or low self-worth, present for most of the day for at least two weeks.

title: Depressive disorder (depression) - WHO fact sheet
section: Depression versus everyday mood changes, and that effective treatment exists
text: Depression is different from ordinary mood fluctuations and short-lived emotional reactions to everyday life. Effective psychological and medication-based treatments exist for mild, moderate, and severe presentations.

title: Depressive disorder (depression) - WHO fact sheet
section: Physical illness, suicide risk and seeking care early
text: Depression can occur alongside physical illness, and untreated depression increases the risk of suicide. WHO recommends timely care-seeking rather than waiting for symptoms to resolve on their own.

title: Depression - NIMH health topic
text: NIMH describes major depressive disorder as going beyond everyday sadness: symptoms are severe enough to interfere with sleeping, eating, working, and relationships.

title: Depression - NIMH health topic
section: Causes and risk factors of depression
text: Contributing factors are thought to be a combination of genetic, biological, environmental, and psychological influences, rather than any single cause.

title: Depression - NIMH health topic
text: Presentations vary between individuals; NIMH describes subtypes such as seasonal patterns and depression with psychotic features.

title: Depression - NIMH health topic
text: Evidence-based treatments include psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioral therapy, antidepressant medication, and sometimes other interventions, typically used in combination under clinical supervision.

title: Depression - MedlinePlus
section: Depression is an illness, not a personal weakness
text: Depression is a mood disorder, not a personal weakness or something a person can simply snap out of.

title: Depression - MedlinePlus
text: Commonly reported symptoms include ongoing sadness or emptiness, irritability, changes in appetite or weight, sleep disturbance, fatigue, and difficulty concentrating, present most of the day nearly every day.

title: Depression - MedlinePlus
section: When to see a doctor or healthcare provider
text: MedlinePlus encourages speaking with a healthcare provider if symptoms persist for more than two weeks or interfere with daily functioning, since earlier treatment is associated with better outcomes.

title: Depression in adults: treatment and management (NG222) - NICE
section: What the NICE adult depression guideline covers
text: NICE guideline NG222 covers identifying, treating, and managing depression in adults aged 18 and over in the UK. It is written for use by clinicians and is not an automatically executable clinical policy.

title: Depression in adults: treatment and management (NG222) - NICE
text: For less severe depression, NICE suggests clinicians discuss low-intensity options first, such as guided self-help, group cognitive behavioural therapy, or structured exercise, before routinely offering antidepressants, based on patient preference.

title: Depression in adults: treatment and management (NG222) - NICE
text: For more severe depression, NICE recommends clinicians consider combining psychological therapy with antidepressant medication, along with closer monitoring.

title: Depression in adults: treatment and management (NG222) - NICE
section: Shared decision-making between patient and clinician about treatment
text: NICE stresses shared decision-making between clinician and patient and ongoing review over time, rather than a one-time automated judgement.
